title: HTTP carrier optimizer and fingerprint-based sampling adapter for low-noise tracing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Production tracing is noisy and costly for high-throughput services where a small percentage of requests generate large spans. Current sampling is either static per-service or relies on downstream heuristics that are inconsistent across platforms. Additionally, we see a lot of span context header bloat and duplicate/incompatible propagation headers across SDKs which increases payload size and complicates downstream collectors.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, cross-language SDK middleware + server-side hook that does two things: (1) computes a stable, low-collision request fingerprint for HTTP/gRPC requests and feeds that into a route-aware adaptive sampler, and (2) normalizes and trims propagation headers into an optimized carrier representation before the request is forwarded or logged. This should reduce trace volume and per-request overhead while keeping high-fidelity traces for high-value traffic.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- SDK middleware for Node and Go (primary) and design notes/extensions for Java/Python. Middleware exposes a small API to opt into: fingerprint keys, per-route sampling overrides, and carrier normalization level.
- Server-side plugin for ingress proxies (Envoy filter prototype) that can compute fingerprint and apply the same carrier optimizer to avoid duplicating SDK work in sidecars.
- Sampling adapter compatible with OpenTelemetry sampling API that accepts fingerprints + route tags and returns decision. Defaults: deterministic stable-sampling for non-error requests, aggressive capture for error/latency signals.
- Carrier optimizer converts multiple propagation headers (traceparent, b3, custom X-RD-*) into a single compact carrier header used internally; preserves full original headers in debug mode.
- Backwards-compatible: when optimizer not enabled, SDKs must continue to forward existing headers unchanged. OTEL header compatibility mode must be available.
- Runtime-configurable via existing config service so sampling rates and route rules can update without full deploy.
- End-to-end tests and benchmarks show <=2% median added latency and at least 40% reduction in traced requests for a default medium-traffic workload.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Design and prototype (2 wks): fingerprint definition, collision tests, carrier proto, sampling decision schema. Artifact: design doc + deterministic test harness.
2) SDK middleware v1 (Node, Go) (3 wks): middleware packages, config hooks, unit tests, CI.
3) Envoy filter prototype (2 wks): proof-of-concept filter to demonstrate server-side fingerprint and carrier optimization.
4) OTEL sampler adapter (2 wks): sampling adapter implementing OTEL interface for runtime decisions.
5) Integration and rollout (2 wks): enable in staging services, run capture vs baseline, update dashboards and alerts.

Key design decisions considered so far:
- Fingerprint composition: request path template + method + host + first N bytes of body hash for POSTs when content-type is json/text. Trade-off: privacy vs fidelity. Current choice: omit user-identifiable fields and sample using path/template by default; body-hash only when explicitly enabled.
- Carrier format: single compressed base64 carrier vs compact JSON. Chosen: compact base62-like token that contains a version byte, trace_id, span_id and flags. Provides smallest on-the-wire size while allowing future feature flags.
- Sampling semantics: deterministic sampling for low-error routes to keep stable traces for performance baselines, rule-based overrides for payment/auth routes with higher default retention.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and distribution across 1M synthetic requests.
- Perf bench: Node and Go microbench harness demonstrating p99 latency impact and median overhead.
- Integration tests against Envoy filter with both IPv4 and IPv6 requests.
- QA rollout: 2% traffic in staging -> 10% in production on non-critical services -> ramp with Canary until thresholds met.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New Console dashboard card: "Fingerprint Sampling Effectiveness" showing sampled vs accepted traces by route, traces removed by optimizer, and per-route collision rate.
- Latency/Error dashboard overlay to ensure optimizer is not dropping error traces.
- Alert: if sampled trace count drops >30% vs baseline for a service in 1h, auto-disable optimizer for that service and notify on-call.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Default disabled for all accounts; enable per-service via Console toggle or runtime config.
- Canary: enable on internal services first (auth, routing), validate alerts.
- Fallback: SDKs include an opt-out and debug header to dump original propagation headers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: fingerprint collisions causing unrelated requests to be sampled together. Mitigation: conservative fingerprint (include route template and method), collision monitoring and ability to switch to higher-fidelity fingerprint.
- Risk: carrier normalization breaks third-party middleware expecting full headers. Mitigation: debug mode preserves headers and we ship compatibility wrappers for common libraries.
- Risk: increased CPU on hot paths. Mitigation: highly-optimized hashing (xxh3) and sampling decision cache.

Open questions:
- Should fingerprint include query parameters for search endpoints? (Trade-off: higher cardinality vs diagnostic value.)
- What is the privacy policy for body-derived fingerprints? Need legal/security signoff.

- Start legal/security review for any body-based fingerprint usage (owner: Priya Nair).
